prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural‑language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject(s), visible actions and interactions, and the setting. Use specific action verbs and name clear maneuvers; for every motion give horizontal direction first (toward/away/left‑to‑right/right‑to‑left/past) then vertical (upward/downward) and indicate the action phase when visible (starting/ascending/peaking/descending/landing) and whether motions are simultaneous or sequential. For interactions with objects or structures state exactly how the subject is using them (holding/pulling/supporting/securing/bracing/leaning on), include hand and side when visible, and describe gestures with target and direction. For all other moving subjects describe their movement relative to the main subject (passing to his right, approaching from behind, moving alongside) and specify whether they are in front of, behind, next to, or overlapping. Describe body posture with concrete camera‑relative terms (standing, slightly leaning forward/back, seated, reclining, crouching, mid‑jump, arms outstretched, knees bent) and specify orientation to the camera (facing the camera, in profile, back to the camera). Report facial expressions or visible affect only when clearly evident using observable detail (open‑mouthed, smiling with teeth visible, furrowed brow) and identify gaze targets (eyes looking up at the kite, gaze fixed on the camera). Clarify precise spatial relationships, count and arrangement of people or vehicles (two people side by side, a row of three boats), proximity and scale (a few feet/meters apart, clustered closely, towering behind), and avoid ambiguous “above” by using “in front of,” “over,” or “directly above/overhead.” Describe lighting and shadows with observable cues (bright direct sunlight, diffuse overcast, directional backlight), where shadows fall and approximate direction or length (casting long shadows toward the lower left), and note visible surface textures or effects when present (wet pavement, puddles, splashes, reflections, motion blur, dust). Keep the caption concrete and image‑centered, avoid speculation or subjective judgments, and output exactly one single sentence.
